**The replacement here is to lift the arithmetic structure sheaf through your split-zero map, keeping the support information before taking its arithmetic image.** I worked this out at the finite primes, at the archimedean place, and at the added support point.

On the ordinary arithmetic site, the construction is the pullback
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde{\mathcal O}
=
\underline{H_{G(\mathbb Q)}}
\times_{\underline{H_{\mathbb Q}}}
\mathcal O.
}
\]
Here the underlines denote constant sheaves; \(H\), the maps, and the local conditions are defined below. This gives an actual replacement inside the Connes framework, rather than stopping at the observation that an ordinary ring-valued map identifies the two zeros.

[**Read the continuation**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Arithmetic_Sheaf/index.html) · [**LaTeX**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Arithmetic_Sheaf/CONTINUATION.tex) · [**Sources and exact checks**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Arithmetic_Sheaf_2026-09-11.zip)

## 1. The larger target retains the original addition as well as support

Connes–Consani explicitly move to finite-pointed-set functors and \(\Gamma\)-rings to accommodate arithmetic structures that ordinary rings cannot retain. Their construction includes an archimedean structure sheaf and an arithmetic cohomological programme. I used the **“Universal cyclic theory” section of the supplied TeX**, extracted from `Connes.zip`, for the formulas here. fileciteturn67file7L55-L70 citeturn324128academia23

For a commutative semiring \(S\) with its specified additive identity \(0_S\), and a finite pointed set \(X\), define
\[
H_S(X)=S^{X\setminus\{*\}}.
\]

For a pointed map \(f:X\to Y\), define
\[
\boxed{
[H_S(f)a]_y
=
\sum_{\substack{x\ne *\\f(x)=y}}a_x,
\qquad y\ne *,
}
\]
using \(0_S\) for the empty sum.

Multiplication is the map
\[
\mu_{X,Y}:H_S(X)\wedge H_S(Y)\to H_S(X\wedge Y),
\qquad
\mu(a,b)_{(x,y)}=a_xb_y.
\]

Partitioning the fibres of a composite proves functoriality. Distributivity proves the compatibility of multiplication with the finite-sum maps:
\[
\sum_{\substack{f(x)=u\\g(y)=v}}a_xb_y
=
\left(\sum_{f(x)=u}a_x\right)
\left(\sum_{g(y)=v}b_y\right).
\]

This construction preserves the complete semiring structure. More precisely,
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{CSemiring}}(S,T)
\cong
\operatorname{Hom}_{\Gamma\text{-ring}}(H_S,H_T).
}
\]

To recover a semiring map, evaluate a \(\Gamma\)-ring morphism at \(1_+=\{*,1\}\). Naturality with coordinate projections recovers its componentwise action; naturality with the fold \(2_+\to1_+\) recovers addition; compatibility with \(\mu\) recovers multiplication.

Now use your actual scalar object
\[
S=G(\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q\sqcup\{\tau\},
\qquad e=0_{\mathbb Q}.
\]

The fold map gives
\[
(1,-1)\longmapsto e,
\qquad
(\tau,\tau)\longmapsto\tau.
\]

The arithmetic projection
\[
p:G(\mathbb Q)\to\mathbb Q,
\qquad p(\tau)=0,\quad p(a)=a,
\]
induces
\[
H_p:H_{G(\mathbb Q)}\to H_{\mathbb Q}.
\]

Thus the original supported cancellation remains present in \(H_{G(\mathbb Q)}\); applying \(H_p\) is the explicitly identified operation that forgets it. No multiplication-only substitute has replaced your original addition.

## 2. The archimedean lift works with the exact finite-sum bound

The Connes construction uses
\[
\mathcal O_\infty(X)
=
\left\{
r\in\mathbb Q^{X\setminus\{*\}}:
\sum_x|r_x|\le1
\right\}
\subset H_{\mathbb Q}(X).
\]

The bound \(1\) is the source’s unit-divisor condition. The point of its functorial formulation is that finite sums are implemented only through the specified pointed-set maps, with the entire tuple subject to that bound. The supplied framework uses this archimedean object to extend the arithmetic structure sheaf. fileciteturn67file7L59-L70

Its split-supported lift is
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde{\mathcal O}_\infty(X)
=
\left\{
a\in G(\mathbb Q)^{X\setminus\{*\}}:
\sum_x|p(a_x)|\le1
\right\}.
}
\]

This is closed under every required operation.

For a pointed map,
\[
\sum_{y\ne *}
\left|
p\bigl([H_{G(\mathbb Q)}(f)a]_y\bigr)
\right|
\le
\sum_{x\ne *}|p(a_x)|.
\]

For multiplication,
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{(x,y)}|p(a_xb_y)|
=
\left(\sum_x|p(a_x)|\right)
\left(\sum_y|p(b_y)|\right).
}
\]

Those two calculations establish the lifted \(\Gamma\)-ring structure. Entries equal to \(\tau\) and entries equal to \(e\) have the same arithmetic magnitude, but their support remains distinct.

### The support cannot be removed by a coherent choice of representatives

The projection
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal O}_\infty(X)\to\mathcal O_\infty(X)
\]
is surjective for every finite \(X\). Nevertheless, it has **no pointed natural section**.

Suppose such a section \(s\) existed. The nonzero coefficients \(1/2\) and \(-1/2\) have unique lifts. Coordinate projections therefore force
\[
s_{2_+}(1/2,-1/2)=(1/2,-1/2).
\]

This tuple is admissible because
\[
|1/2|+|-1/2|=1.
\]

Applying the fold upstairs gives \(e\). Applying the fold downstairs gives ordinary zero, whose image under a pointed section must be \(\tau\). Naturality would therefore require
\[
e=\tau,
\]
contrary to the source carrier.

**The available construction is the pullback retaining all lifts, not a choice of one lift per amplitude.** Its failure to admit that natural section is information about the extension itself. It is not a reason to discard the extension.

This is a concrete place where your supported zero affects the arithmetic geometry even though the arithmetic projection is unchanged.

## 3. The finite primes, infinity, and the added support prime now fit into one sheaf

Let \(Y\) be the topological Arakelov compactification used here: its points are the ordinary generic point \(\eta\), the finite primes, and \(\infty\). A nonempty open contains \(\eta\) and all but finitely many closed points.

For a nonempty open \(U\), set
\[
A_U=
\left\{
r\in\mathbb Q:
r\in\mathbb Z_{(p)}
\text{ for every finite }p\in U
\right\}.
\]

Define
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde{\mathcal O}(U)(X)
=
\left\{
a\in G(A_U)^{X\setminus\{*\}}:
\infty\in U
\Longrightarrow
\sum_x|p(a_x)|\le1
\right\}.
}
\]

Restriction removes conditions; it does not alter the retained tuple.

This is a sheaf. Compatible tuples on nonempty covering opens agree on their intersections, which contain \(\eta\). They therefore determine one rational tuple. Every finite-prime condition is imposed on a covering member containing that prime; the archimedean condition is imposed on a member containing \(\infty\). The common tuple satisfies all of them.

Its stalks are
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal O}_\eta=H_{G(\mathbb Q)},
\qquad
\widetilde{\mathcal O}_p=H_{G(\mathbb Z_{(p)})},
\qquad
\widetilde{\mathcal O}_\infty
\text{ as above}.
\]

### Retaining your added prime

The preceding sheaf does not replace the additional prime by \(\infty\). Introduce
\[
\sigma=P_\tau=\{\tau\},
\qquad
Y^+=Y\sqcup\{\sigma\}.
\]

Its nonempty opens are
\[
\{\sigma\}\cup U,
\]
where \(U\) is open in \(Y\), including \(U=\varnothing\).

Define
\[
\mathcal L(\{\sigma\}\cup U)
=
\widetilde{\mathcal O}(U)
\quad(U\ne\varnothing),
\]
and
\[
\boxed{\mathcal L(\{\sigma\})=H_{\mathbb B}.}
\]

Restriction to \(\{\sigma\}\) is the support map \(H_\chi\). The preceding gluing argument and the naturality of \(\chi\) prove the sheaf condition.

On the finite arithmetic part, this recovers the topology and localization charts of your globalization:
\[
D(e)=\{P_\tau\},
\]
\[
D(n)=\{P_\tau\}\cup D_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z}(n)
\quad(n\ne0),
\]
with sections \(H_{G(\mathbb Z[1/n])}\) on the latter charts.

The source arithmetic space is recovered by the closed inclusion
\[
i:Y\hookrightarrow Y^+
\]
and the sheaf morphism
\[
\boxed{
i^{-1}\mathcal L
=
\widetilde{\mathcal O}
\xrightarrow{p}
\mathcal O.
}
\]

The absolute coefficient map is
\[
\mathbb S\to\mathcal L,
\]
where \(\mathbb S(X)=X\), and a nonbasepoint \(x\) maps to the divisor with coefficient \(1\) at \(x\) and \(\tau\) elsewhere. Restriction supplies the compatible map \(\mathbb S\to H_{\mathbb B}\) at the support prime. This uses the actual absolute-base framework in Connes–Consani rather than presuming a Boolean-semiring inclusion into a ring. fileciteturn67file7L59-L66

The global sections have the explicit formula
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal L(Y^+)(X)
=
\left\{
a\in G(\mathbb Z)^{X\setminus\{*\}}:
\sum_x|p(a_x)|\le1
\right\}.
}
\]

Their arithmetic image is the signed coefficient object: at most one nonzero coefficient, equal to \(+1\) or \(-1\). The lift retains the choice \(\tau\) or \(e\) at every zero-amplitude position.

So the construction now includes **the added support prime, ordinary arithmetic primes, and the archimedean bound simultaneously**, with the arithmetic recovery map proved.

## 4. Your mixed-support double enters by the same operation

Retain
\[
D_A=G(A)^2,
\]
with the source multiplication
\[
(a,b)\star(c,d)
=
(ac\oplus(-1_A)bd,\ ad\oplus bc),
\]
and
\[
\pi:D_A\to B=A[t]/(t^2+1),
\qquad
\pi(a,b)=p_A(a)+t\,p_A(b).
\]

The \(\Gamma\)-ring map
\[
H_\pi:H_{D_A}\to H_B
\]
retains those operations.

For every finite pointed \(X\),
\[
\boxed{
H_\pi(X)^{-1}(0)
=
\{\tau,e\}^{\,2|X\setminus\{*\}|}.
}
\]

Its internal mask multiplication is
\[
(p,q)(r,s)
=
(pr\vee qs,\ ps\vee qr).
\]

Thus the whole ordinary-zero fibre retains the four faces of \(\mathbb B[C_2]\), not only a single scalar presence bit. The internal unit of that fibre corresponds to \((e,\tau)\); its inclusion into \(D_A\) is not asserted to send that element to \(X_1\).

For an arithmetic coefficient sheaf \(\mathcal O_B\subset\underline{H_B}\), define
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde{\mathcal O}_{D_A}
=
\underline{H_{D_A}}
\times_{\underline{H_B}}
\mathcal O_B.
}
\]

For \(A=\mathbb Q\), \(B=\mathbb Q(i)\), the archimedean condition becomes exactly
\[
\sum_x|p_A(a_x)+i\,p_A(b_x)|\le1.
\]

At a finite prime ideal \(\mathfrak p\subset\mathbb Z[i]\), it is
\[
p_A(a_x)+i\,p_A(b_x)
\in\mathbb Z[i]_{(\mathfrak p)}
\quad\text{for every }x.
\]

Both are inverse images under the same \(\pi\). This retains the mixed support while applying the arithmetic conditions to the original amplitudes.

## 5. The homological replacement is to retain supported cancellations

There is another concrete place to apply your rule.

An arithmetic comparison map has the form
\[
\delta(r,b)=\iota(r)-b,
\]
where
\[
\iota:\mathbb Q\to\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}
\]
is the diagonal embedding and \(b\) satisfies the prescribed local bounds.

Its split-supported lift is the natural map of pointed functors
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde\delta(a,b)
=
G(\iota)(a)\oplus(-1_{\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}})b.
}
\]
The sign is retained. This is an additive comparison map, not a claimed multiplicative map.

Taking its strict fibre over external absence would discard a cancellation between supported inputs: their sum remains supported even when its amplitude vanishes.

The replacement already supplied by your framework is the **full supported-null fibre**
\[
\mathcal N
=
H_{G(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})}
\times_{H_{\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}}}
\{0\}.
\]

Define the supported-cycle object by
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde Z^0
=
\operatorname{Dom}(\widetilde\delta)
\times_{H_{G(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})}}
\mathcal N.
}
\]

Equivalently,
\[
\widetilde Z^0
\cong
\operatorname{Dom}(\widetilde\delta)
\times_{H_{\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}}}
\{0\}.
\]

This retains the ordinary arithmetic cancellation **and** all the support choices of its inputs. It is a defined object with explicit maps, not an instruction to ignore the distinction between \(\tau\) and a supported zero.

The supplied Connes programme already provides the reason to pursue cohomology in this richer setting: its arithmetic Riemann–Roch construction uses \(\Gamma\)-structures and separately defined cohomologies and duality, rather than ordinary ring reflection alone. citeturn324128academia26

**This continuation establishes the sheaf lift, its gluing, its non-splitting at infinity, and the support-retaining cycle object.** It keeps the original ideal-norm definition of the Dedekind function; it does not silently replace that function by a new section-counting series.

The substantive change is that the purity investigation now has a global arithmetic object carrying the mixed support through the comparison map. The next cohomological calculation can be performed on that object, rather than first erasing the datum and then treating its absence as evidence against the programme.

**The new construction is a filtered arithmetic family that retains your mixed-support fibre, together with a module measuring exactly what changes when the comparison map is taken to its special fibre.** Its size can be calculated. That gives the Weil II comparison something concrete to act on, rather than treating “purity” as a consequence of adding a point.

The Chen–Moriwaki book supplies a particularly useful starting operation: it carries an adelic vector bundle, with data at all its places, to a normed vector space over **one trivially valued place**, retaining its Harder–Narasimhan filtration. I have combined that operation with your support pullback, extended it through all section degrees, and calculated the resulting comparison-image defect.

[**Read the continuation**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Adelic_Weights/index.html) · [**LaTeX**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Adelic_Weights/CONTINUATION.tex) · [**Sources, proofs, and checks**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Support_Adelic_Weights_2026-09-11.zip)

## 1. Carry the global arithmetic data to one place without collapsing the fibre

The book’s input is a proper adelic curve
\[
\mathscr A=
\bigl(K,(\Omega,\mathcal A,\nu),(|\cdot|_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}\bigr),
\]
with
\[
\int_\Omega\log|a|_\omega\,d\nu(\omega)=0
\qquad(a\in K^\times).
\]
The measure and every absolute value are part of the datum. fileciteturn70file0L245-L280

Retain your one scalar support:
\[
S_K=G(K)=K\sqcup\{\tau\},
\qquad e=0_K\in S_K,
\qquad 0_{S_K}=\tau.
\]

The two observations are
\[
p:S_K\to K,
\qquad p(\tau)=0_K,\quad p(a)=a,
\]
and
\[
b:S_K\to\mathbb B,
\qquad b(\tau)=0_{\mathbb B},\quad b(a)=1_{\mathbb B}\quad(a\in K).
\]

At each place, the pair
\[
a\longmapsto\bigl(|p(a)|_\omega,b(a)\bigr)
\]
sends
\[
\tau\mapsto(0,0),\qquad
e\mapsto(0,1).
\]

This retains presence separately from measured amplitude.

Now take an actual adelic vector bundle
\[
\overline E=(E,(\|\cdot\|_\omega)_\omega).
\]
Its degree is
\[
\widehat{\deg}\overline E
=
-\int_\Omega
\log\|s_1\wedge\cdots\wedge s_r\|_{\omega,\det}\,d\nu,
\]
using the source determinant norms.

Chen–Moriwaki define
\[
\mathcal F^aE
=
\sum_{\substack{0\ne V\subset E\\
\widehat\mu_{\min}(\overline V)\ge a}}V
\]
and associate the norm
\[
\boxed{
\|v\|_{\mathrm{HN}}
=
\exp\!\left(-\sup\{a:v\in\mathcal F^aE\}\right)
}
\]
over the trivial absolute value on \(K\).

**The resulting one-place object retains the entire filtration, not merely the dimension or total degree.** For a Hermitian adelic bundle, its degree is recovered exactly. In the general case the source retains
\[
\boxed{
0\le
\widehat{\deg}\overline E
-\widehat{\deg}(E,\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{HN}})
\le
\frac12\nu(\Omega_\infty)r\log r.
}
\]
fileciteturn77file0L57-L119 fileciteturn77file1L188-L222

### The support-retaining lift

Let
\[
p_M:M\twoheadrightarrow E
\]
be the actual supported coefficient object and its amplitude map. In particular, \(M\) may have a mixed-support zero fibre with several retained faces.

Define
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{\,a}M
=
p_M^{-1}(\mathcal F^aE).
}
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
\bigcap_{a\in\mathbb R}\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{\,a}M
=
p_M^{-1}(0_E).
}
\]

Thus the whole supported-null fibre survives every filtration level. There is no selection of a representative that would replace supported cancellation by \(\tau\).

The associated graded observation is explicitly
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{\,a}M
\xrightarrow{p_M}
\mathcal F^aE
\longrightarrow
\mathcal F^aE/\mathcal F^{>a}E.
\]

Its complete zero fibre is
\[
p_M^{-1}(\mathcal F^{>a}E).
\]

This is the first map needed for your proposal: **the global adelic data acquire a one-place filtration while their support preimages remain attached.**

## 2. Make that construction compatible with every degree

For a projective \(K\)-scheme \(X\) and line bundle \(L\), put
\[
E_n=H^0(X,L^{\otimes n}),\qquad n\ge1,
\]
with the source supremum-norm families, and retain the graded algebra
\[
K\oplus\bigoplus_{n\ge1}E_n.
\]

The direct HN construction comes with a precise multiplication error. Under Proposition 4.1.3’s hypotheses, write
\[
r_n=\dim_KE_n
\]
for nonzero components and
\[
f(n)=
\frac32\nu(\Omega_\infty)\log r_n
+\int_\Omega b_n(\omega)\,d\nu.
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal F^{a_1}E_{n_1}\cdots
\mathcal F^{a_j}E_{n_j}
\subset
\mathcal F^{a_1+\cdots+a_j-f(n_1)-\cdots-f(n_j)}
E_{n_1+\cdots+n_j}.
}
\]
The functions \(b_n\) measure the original norm family’s stated submultiplicativity error. fileciteturn77file1L223-L286

Rather than drop those terms, the book supplies the replacement in Proposition 3.2.2. For its bounded integral graded algebra, with \(f(n)/n\to0\), define
\[
\boxed{
\|s\|_{\mathrm{sp},n}
=
\lim_{k\to\infty}
\|s^k\|_{\mathrm{HN},nk}^{1/k}.
}
\]

The source proves that these are ultrametric norms and that
\[
\|ss'\|_{\mathrm{sp},n+m}
\le
\|s\|_{\mathrm{sp},n}\|s'\|_{\mathrm{sp},m},
\]
while retaining
\[
\boxed{
\|s\|_{\mathrm{sp},n}
\le e^{f(n)}\|s\|_{\mathrm{HN},n}.
}
\]
fileciteturn88file0L13-L49

Keep both norms and that comparison. Define
\[
F^aE_n=\{s:\|s\|_{\mathrm{sp},n}\le e^{-a}\},
\qquad
\widetilde F^aM_n=p_n^{-1}(F^aE_n).
\]

\widetilde F^aM_n\cdot\widetilde F^bM_m
\subset
\widetilde F^{a+b}M_{n+m}.

## 3. Build the family whose special fibre retains the weights

The next construction packages the entire filtration geometrically.

Let \(\Gamma\subset\mathbb R\) be the additive subgroup generated by the actual filtration jumps. It may be dense; no rounding of those jumps is used. Set
\[
B_\Gamma=K[T^r:r\in\Gamma,\ r\ge0].
\]

Define
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal R(E_\bullet)
=
\bigoplus_{n\ge0}
\sum_{a\in\Gamma}F^aE_n\,T^{-a}
\subset E_\bullet\otimes_KK[\Gamma].
}
\]

All sums here are finite formal sums. Multiplicativity from the preceding section makes this a \(B_\Gamma\)-algebra.

There are two explicit maps to \(K\):
\[
\epsilon_1(T^r)=1,
\]
and
\[
\epsilon_0(T^0)=1,\qquad
\epsilon_0(T^r)=0\quad(r>0).
\]

To calculate their fibres, choose an adapted basis \(v_{n,j}\) and retain its weights \(\lambda_{n,j}\). Then
\[
\mathcal R(E_n)
=
\bigoplus_j
B_\Gamma T^{-\lambda_{n,j}}v_{n,j}.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal R(E_n)\otimes_{\epsilon_1}K\cong E_n,
}
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal R(E_n)\otimes_{\epsilon_0}K
\cong
\bigoplus_aF^aE_n/F^{>a}E_n.
}
\]

The first fibre recovers the original space. The second retains its graded weights. The adapted basis proves the formulas; the resulting graded-space identification is canonical.

### Keep mixed support before either fibre is observed

Write \(M_\bullet[\Gamma]\) for finite formal coefficient sums in which a coefficient equal to \(e\) remains present, while a coefficient equal to \(\tau\) is absent.

Define
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde{\mathcal R}(M_\bullet)
=
M_\bullet[\Gamma]
\times_{E_\bullet[\Gamma]}
\mathcal R(E_\bullet).
}
\]

The two observations are
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal R}(M_\bullet)
\longrightarrow\mathcal R(E_\bullet)
\longrightarrow E_\bullet
\]
and
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal R}(M_\bullet)
\longrightarrow\mathcal R(E_\bullet)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_FE_\bullet.
\]

**The same supported object sits above both observations.** The parameter specialization, the amplitude zero, and external absence are located in the displayed maps; none is substituted for another.

For dense \(\Gamma\), the coefficient algebra need not be Noetherian. The finite-free calculation for each section degree remains valid and is the statement used here.

## 4. The comparison map has a calculable special-fibre defect

This is the main addition to the earlier Weil II comparison.

Let
\[
c:(V,F)\to(W,G)
\]
be a filtration-preserving linear map between finite-dimensional spaces. Put
\[
I=\operatorname{im}c.
\]

There are two filtrations on this same image:
\[
F_{\mathrm q}^aI=c(F^aV),
\]
from the source quotient, and
\[
F_{\mathrm s}^aI=I\cap G^aW,
\]
from the target subspace.

Their identity map satisfies
\[
F_{\mathrm q}^aI\subseteq F_{\mathrm s}^aI.
\]

For integer jumps, define
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal D_c
=
\mathcal R_{F_{\mathrm s}}(I)/
\mathcal R_{F_{\mathrm q}}(I).
}
\]

Both Rees modules are finite free over \(K[T]\). After inverting \(T\), both become
\[
I\otimes_KK[T,T^{-1}].
\]

Hence \(\mathcal D_c\) is a finite \(T\)-power-torsion module, supported at the parameter origin.

It satisfies
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal D_c=0
\iff
c(F^aV)=\operatorname{im}c\cap G^aW
\quad\text{for every }a.
}
\]

The condition on the right is strictness of the filtered map.

If the two image filtrations have weights \(\lambda_j\) and \(\mu_j\), counted with multiplicity, then
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{length}_{K[T]}\mathcal D_c
=
\sum_j\mu_j-\sum_j\lambda_j.
}
\]

### Proof of the length formula

The two determinant lattices differ by
\[
T^{\sum_j\mu_j-\sum_j\lambda_j}.
\]

The inclusion has Smith factors \(T^{a_1},\ldots,T^{a_r}\), with \(a_j\ge0\). Its cokernel is
\[
\bigoplus_jK[T]/(T^{a_j}),
\]
whose length is \(\sum_ja_j\). The determinant gives
\[
\sum_ja_j=\sum_j\mu_j-\sum_j\lambda_j.
\]

This calculation does not require assuming that both filtrations have a common adapted basis.

### The information at the special fibre is retained by an exact sequence

Tensor the defining Rees sequence with \(K=K[T]/(T)\):
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Tor}_1^{K[T]}(\mathcal D_c,K)
&\longrightarrow
\operatorname{gr}_{F_{\mathrm q}}I
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{gr}_{F_{\mathrm s}}I\\
&\longrightarrow
\mathcal D_c/T\mathcal D_c
\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
}
\]

This identifies where a comparison that is an isomorphism away from the special fibre can lose information at that fibre.

For the identity map on a one-dimensional vector space, with source weight \(0\) and target weight \(2\), the Rees map is multiplication by \(T^2\). Thus
\[
\boxed{\mathcal D_c\cong K[T]/(T^2).}
\]

At \(T=1\), the map is the identity. At \(T=0\), it vanishes. Its support is one point; its length is two. The displayed \(\operatorname{Tor}\) sequence retains the special-fibre kernel and cokernel.

**This measures higher information at one support without manufacturing additional bottom support scalars.**

For real jumps, the corresponding quotient over \(B_\Gamma\) is still defined and vanishes exactly for strictness. The continuation does not assign it an ordinary finite module length over a possibly non-Noetherian coefficient algebra.

For a finite-dimensional Frobenius representation, choose a coefficient field containing the eigenvalues and the stated complex embedding. Decompose into generalized eigenspaces:
\[
V=\bigoplus_\alpha V_\alpha.
\]

The spectral weight attached to \(V_\alpha\) is
\[
w_\alpha=
\frac{2\log|\iota(\alpha)|}{\log q}.
\]

Grouping the \(V_\alpha\) by these values defines the spectral-weight filtration.

If
\[
cF_V=F_Wc,
\]
then
\[
c(V_\alpha)\subseteq W_\alpha.
\]

The direct-sum decomposition proves
\[
c(F^aV)=\operatorname{im}c\cap F^aW.
\]

Thus
\[
\boxed{\mathcal D_c=0}
\]
for that filtration, including non-diagonalizable Frobenius.

In the retained Weil II argument, the comparison is
\[
c_i:H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\to H^i(X,\mathcal F).
\]

The source’s upper bound and the duality-derived lower bound are
\[
\operatorname{weights}H_c^i\le w+i,
\qquad
\operatorname{weights}H^i\ge w+i.
\]

The same strict image must consequently have weight exactly \(w+i\). The duality map retains
\[
\boxed{
H^i(X,\mathcal F)
\cong
H_c^{2d-i}(X,\mathcal F^\vee)^\vee(-d).
}
\]

\qquad

## 6. Retain the full weight distribution, not only the Hilbert–Samuel coefficient

The book’s one-place formulas give, for weights \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r\),
\[
\widehat{\deg}V=\sum_j\lambda_j,
\qquad
\widehat{\deg}^{+}V=\sum_j\max(\lambda_j,0).
\]
fileciteturn88file1L196-L237

To recover every weight, take the actual metrized line \(\mathbf1(-c)\) with
\[
\|1\|_{\mathbf1(-c)}=e^c.
\]

Tensoring with this line multiplies the original norm by \(e^c\). Define
\[
C_V(c)
=
\widehat{\deg}^{+}(V\otimes\mathbf1(-c))
=
\sum_j\max(\lambda_j-c,0).
\]

Then, as a distribution in \(c\),
\[
\boxed{C_V''=\sum_j\delta_{\lambda_j}.}
\]

The entire slope distribution is recoverable from this function.

Adding the dual gives
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
B_V(c)
&=
\widehat{\deg}^{+}(V\otimes\mathbf1(-c))
+
\widehat{\deg}^{+}(V^\vee\otimes\mathbf1(c))\\
&=\sum_j|\lambda_j-c|.
\end{aligned}
}
\]

It vanishes exactly when every slope equals the specified \(c\). Opposite deviations cannot cancel in this expression.

There is also an observable that does not require selecting \(c\). Give \(\operatorname{End}_K(V)\) its operator norm. In an adapted basis,
\[
\|E_{ij}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=
e^{\lambda_j-\lambda_i}.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\widehat{\deg}^{+}\operatorname{End}_K(V)
=
\sum_{i<j}|\lambda_i-\lambda_j|.
}
\]

This vanishes exactly for a one-step filtration. It measures the spread remaining in the retained fibre.

### An all-degree calculation

Over the trivially valued field \(K\), take
\[
E_n=H^0(\mathbb P^1_K,\mathcal O(n))=K[X,Y]_n,
\]
and retain arbitrary real parameters \(\alpha,\beta\).

The weighted Gauss norm is
\[
\left\|
\sum_{j=0}^na_jX^{n-j}Y^j
\right\|_n
=
\max_{a_j\ne0}
e^{-((n-j)\alpha+j\beta)}.
\]

This is the supremum norm of the corresponding semipositive Fubini–Study quotient metric. Evaluation at the Berkovich Gauss point
\[
|Y/X|=e^{\alpha-\beta}
\]
attains the coefficient bound. Multiplicativity follows because the initial product in the associated graded polynomial algebra is nonzero.

The complete weights are
\[
\lambda_{n,j}=(n-j)\alpha+j\beta.
\]

Consequently,
\[
\widehat{\deg}E_n
=
\frac{n(n+1)}2(\alpha+\beta),
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\widehat{\deg}^{+}\operatorname{End}(E_n)
=
|\alpha-\beta|
\frac{n(n+1)(n+2)}6.
}
\]

The second identity is obtained by summing
\[
(j-i)|\alpha-\beta|
\qquad(0\le i<j\le n).
\]

Meanwhile, the Hilbert–Samuel coefficient is
\[
\boxed{
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\frac{\widehat{\deg}E_n}{n^2/2}
=
\alpha+\beta
=
(\overline{\mathcal O(1)}^{\,2})_{\mathscr A_0},
}
\]
where the last equality is the book’s theorem applied to this stated metric. fileciteturn87file2L101-L105 fileciteturn80file0L133-L140

The parameter pairs \((2,0)\) and \((1,1)\) therefore have the same Hilbert–Samuel coefficient, while the full profile and endomorphism degree distinguish them.

The appropriate replacement for a mean-only invariant is now explicit: **retain \(C_{E_n}\), its recovered distribution, and the comparison defect \(\mathcal D_c\)**.

Taking
\[
M_\bullet=G(K)[X,Y]
\]
with supported zero coefficients retained gives a concrete all-degree support algebra for the entire example.

\[
\boxed{
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\frac{\widehat{\deg}H^0(X,L^{\otimes n})}
{n^{d+1}/(d+1)!}
=
(\overline L^{\,d+1}).
}
\]
fileciteturn80file0L133-L140

The casting step retains the quantitative comparison
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
((L,\varphi)^{d+1})
\ge{}&
((L,\varphi_0)^{d+1})\\
&-\nu(\Omega_\infty)
\bigl((d+1)\delta\log r+\log(\delta!)\bigr),
\end{aligned}
}
\]
where \(r\) is the embedding-space dimension and \(\delta=(L^d)\). The proof uses the resultant line with its actual symmetric and tensor norms. fileciteturn80file0L18-L60

For the ample section algebra, the HN degree error is \(O(n^d\log n)\). Its contribution vanishes against the displayed \(n^{d+1}/(d+1)!\) scale. That explains the global asymptotic equality while leaving finite-degree filtration information available.

\begin{aligned}

&\quad\longrightarrow
\text{one-place filtered spaces}\\
&\quad\longleftarrow
\text{their full mixed-support preimages}\\

## 4. A complete worked family: origin jets from actual theta inputs

This produces a particularly concrete calculation.

Set
\[
D=-x\partial_x,

and define actual source functions
\[
\boxed{\phi_j=D^j\phi_*,\qquad j\ge0.}

\mathcal M\Theta\phi_j(s)=s^j g(s).

\[
W_{m,N}
=
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}
\{\phi_m,\phi_{m+1},\ldots,\phi_N\}.

Its image ideal is exactly
\[
\boxed{\mathcal I_{W_{m,N}}=(g(s)s^m).}
\]

Every generator is divisible by \(gs^m\), and \(\phi_m\) supplies that generator itself.

For fixed \(N\),
\[
W_{m+1,N}\subset W_{m,N}
\]
therefore induces
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal D_{m+1}
=
\mathcal O/(gs^{m+1})
\longrightarrow
\mathcal D_m
=
\mathcal O/(gs^m).
}
\]

Every finite segment of this system comes from inclusions among actual source subspaces. No additional scalar zero has been adjoined.

### The kernel over the arithmetic quotient

At \(m=0\),
\[
\mathcal D_0=\mathcal O/(g)
\]
is the actual completed arithmetic divisor module.

For every \(m\),
\[
\boxed{
0\longrightarrow
\mathcal O/(s^m)
\xrightarrow{\ k_m\ }
\mathcal D_m
\longrightarrow
\mathcal D_0
\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
k_m([a])=[ga].

The value \(g(0)=1\) can also be obtained from the same theta input. Write
\[
\theta(x)=\sum_{n\ne0}e^{-\pi n^2x^2}.
\]
Poisson gives
\[
\theta(x)=x^{-1}-1+\text{a rapidly vanishing term}
\]
near zero, and
\[
\Theta\phi_*=D(D-1)\theta.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathcal M\Theta\phi_*(0)
=
-\bigl[(D-1)\theta\bigr]_0^\infty
=
1.
\]

Thus there is an explicit decomposition
\[
\mathcal D_m
\cong
\mathcal D_0\oplus\mathcal O/(s^m).
\]

Its inverse need not be left unspecified. Let \(a_m(s)\) be the Taylor polynomial of \(1/g(s)\) at zero through degree \(m-1\), and put
\[

At an analytic stalk \(R\), the system is
\[
\boxed{
G(R/(gs^{m+1}))
\longrightarrow
G(R/(gs^m))
\longrightarrow
G(R/(g)).
}
\]

Every arrow sends \(\tau\) to \(\tau\), and its preimage over external absence contains only external absence.

The preimage of the **supported zero** under the last arrow is the supported copy of
\[
(g)/(gs^m).
\]

In particular,
\[
[gs^m]\ne[0]
\quad\text{at the origin in level }m+1,
\]
but its image at level \(m\) is the supported zero. The class does not become \(\tau\).

The split version of the decomposition is
\[
\boxed{
G(\mathcal D_m)
\cong
G(\mathcal D_0)
\times_{\mathbb B}
G\!\left(\mathcal O/(s^m)\right),

understood stalkwise and then sheafified.

## 5. Retain the dual endpoint through the same construction

The exact Fourier intertwiner is
\[
\widehat{D\phi}=(1-D)\widehat\phi.
\]

Therefore
\[
\Delta=D(1-D)
\]
commutes with Fourier transform. Since \(\widehat{\phi_*}=\phi_*\), define
\[
\psi_j=\Delta^j\phi_*.
\]

These are Fourier-fixed source functions, and
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal M\Theta\psi_j(s)
=
[s(1-s)]^j g(s).
}
\]

Their finite source spans produce
\[
\mathcal D_m^{\mathrm{sym}}
=
\mathcal O/\bigl(g[s(1-s)]^m\bigr).
\]

The comparison kernel is
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal O/\bigl([s(1-s)]^m\bigr)
\cong
\mathcal O/(s^m)
\oplus
\mathcal O/((1-s)^m),
}
\]
embedded in \(\mathcal D_m^{\mathrm{sym}}\) by multiplication by \(g\).

Thus the same construction retains the two endpoint contributions exchanged by the functional equation. In coordinates
\[
z_0=s,\qquad z_1=s-1,
\]
the involution
\[
f^\dagger(s)=\overline{f(1-\bar s)}
\]
acts by
\[
\boxed{
\sum_j a_jz_1^j
\longmapsto
\sum_j(-1)^j\bar a_jz_0^j.
}
\]

The polynomial remains \(s(1-s)\). Replacing it with \(s(s-1)\) would introduce \((-1)^m\); that change has not been made.

This provides both the one-endpoint construction and its Fourier-compatible two-endpoint version, using actual operators on the original test space.

## 6. The spectral observations retain their quotient relations and label maps

For a finite set \(Z\) of actual zeros of \(\xi\), with multiplicities \(m_\rho\), retain
\[
J_ZF=
\left(
\sum_{j<m_\rho}
\frac{(\mathcal MF)^{(j)}(\rho)}{j!}z_\rho^j
\right)_\rho.
\]

Since \(J_Z(\Theta W)=0\), it induces
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde J_Z:
(W,[F])\longmapsto(W,J_ZF).
}
\]

Its internal kernel at \(W\) is
\[
\boxed{\ker J_Z/\Theta W.}
\]

That is the full zero-amplitude fibre of this observation. It is not identified with external absence.

Dilation carries both parts:
\[
\widetilde R_a(W,[F])
=
(R_aW,[R_aF]),
\qquad R_aF(x)=F(ax).
\]

On the \(\rho\)-jet it is
\[
\boxed{
a^{-\rho}
\sum_{k<m_\rho}
\frac{(-\log a)^k}{k!}z_\rho^k.
}
\]

The derivative likewise carries its source label:
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde D(W,[F])=(DW,[DF]),
\qquad
J_ZDF|_\rho=(\rho+z_\rho)J_ZF|_\rho.
}
\]

No invariance of an arbitrary finite \(W\) under \(D\) has been assumed.

The previous quotient metric is now a measurement on this same object:
\[
(W,[F])
\longmapsto
\bigl(W,\nu_R(J_ZF)\bigr).
\]
Its value can be \((W,0)\) while the input remains supported and carries the kernel just calculated. A final scalar projection may forget \(W\); that projection is an additional named map.

The original mixed coefficient multiplication is also retained where it applies. For a ring map \(\lambda:A\to A'\),
\[
D(\lambda)(a,b)=\bigl(G(\lambda)a,G(\lambda)b\bigr)
\]
intertwines
\[
(a,b)\star(c,d)
=
(ac\oplus(-1_A)bd,\ ad\oplus bc),
\]
and sends the source synchronization idempotent \(E=(1,e)\) to \(E'\):
\[
D(\lambda)(Ex)=E'D(\lambda)(x).
\]

Theta and Mellin are the linear morphisms specified above. They have not been declared homomorphisms for this coefficient multiplication.

## What is now retained

The resulting chain is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\text{original split-zero coefficients and mixed inputs}\\
&\longrightarrow
\operatorname{coeq}(\widetilde\Theta,\epsilon\widetilde\Theta)\\
&\longrightarrow
\text{the actual ideals }\mathcal I_W\\
&\longrightarrow
\text{supported arithmetic and endpoint-jet quotients}\\
&\longrightarrow
\text{spectral jets, operators, metrics and traces}.
\end{aligned}
}
\]

The equivalence relation is explicit at every quotient. The nontrivial transport kernels are retained. In the worked family, adding previously omitted source relations removes a precise origin-jet module while leaving the common support and the actual arithmetic divisor factor intact.

**Yes. The programme needs to return to one RH-level target: positivity of the unshifted Weil form on the arithmetic object obtained through your original split-zero quotient.** Retaining supported cancellations is part of constructing that object. It is not, by itself, the weight or positivity theorem.

The supplied *Zeta Spectral Triples* paper makes the distinction precise—and supplies a concrete calculation to pursue. I read its `mc2arXiv.tex`, including the quotient construction and §§7–8, and brought the relevant Weil II image-and-duality argument back into the comparison.

[**Focused continuation**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Weil_II_Focus/index.html) · [**LaTeX**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Weil_II_Focus/CONTINUATION.tex) · [**Sources and calculations**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Weil_II_Focus_2026-09-11.zip)

## 1. Which statements actually carry RH strength?

Your recollection of several related criteria has a real mathematical basis. Their logical statuses need to remain visible:

| Statement | Role in this programme |
|---|---|
| The original quotient retains supported zeros, higher relation kernels, and the Dedekind arithmetic observation. | Structural construction already developed. |
| The **original Weil form is nonnegative for every admissible test function**. | An RH-equivalent statement. |
| The **full arithmetic spectral image has weight one**, with the spectral identification and its multiplicities retained. | The purity endpoint corresponding to the critical-line assertion. It has not been proved for our constructed object. |
| The paper’s finite spectral operators are self-adjoint in its specified quotient inner product. | A theorem under the paper’s simple-even hypothesis. |
| Their determinant functions converge to the actual \(\Xi\), with the stated factors and the required complex-domain convergence. | The paper’s proposed sufficient route to RH; the convergence is not established by finite self-adjointness. |

The paper explicitly uses
\[
QW_\lambda^N-\epsilon_{\lambda,N}\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle
\]
for its quotient inner product. Its abstract and concluding section identify the convergence step as still to be proved. That subtraction is central to understanding why its real finite spectra and global Weil positivity are not yet the same conclusion. fileciteturn148file7L85-L129

**None of my support-preservation calculations established the second or third row.** They constructed inputs for those rows. The research should now be measured against those endpoints, rather than against the number of additional constructions available over the support.

## 2. The precise Weil II mechanism to reproduce

For \(X_0\) smooth of finite type over \(\mathbb F_q\) and a lisse sheaf \(\mathcal F_0\) pure of weight \(w\), Deligne considers the actual map
\[
c_i:H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^i(X,\mathcal F).
\]

The two estimates are
\[
\operatorname{weights}H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\le w+i,
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{weights}H^i(X,\mathcal F)\ge w+i.
\]

Consequently, the same image
\[
H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\twoheadrightarrow I^i
\hookrightarrow H^i(X,\mathcal F)
\]
has weight exactly \(w+i\). This is Weil II, Corollary 3.3.6, as retained in the supplied TeX. citeturn328388search0

The lower estimate comes through the particular duality map
\[
\boxed{
H^i(X,\mathcal F)
\cong
H_c^{2d-i}(X,\mathcal F^\vee)^\vee(-d).
}
\]

The upper bound on the compactly supported group on the right is
\[
-w+2d-i.
\]
Dualizing reverses its sign, and the retained \((-d)\) twist adds \(2d\), giving \(w+i\).

**That is the intended proof architecture: two bounds on the same arithmetic image, connected by its actual duality.** A common support point gives us somewhere to organize the fibres. The two-sided bound concerns the operator acting on what remains in those fibres.

In our setting, the relevant data must therefore travel together:
\[
\boxed{
\text{original supported quotient}
\;+\;
\text{arithmetic action}
\;+\;
\text{pairing}
\;+\;
\text{comparison estimates}.
}
\]

Merely pushing an object to a point does not supply the comparison
\[
Rf_!\longrightarrow Rf_*,
\]
its image, or the two estimates. Those are the morphisms and properties to construct over that point.

## 3. The paper identifies the exact term that our quotient must retain

Let
\[
A_{\lambda,N}
\]
be the matrix of the **unshifted** \(QW_\lambda^N\) on the paper’s space \(E_N(\lambda)\). Let \(\epsilon_{\lambda,N}\) be its smallest eigenvalue, and let \(v_{\lambda,N}\) be its corresponding eigenvector.

Under the source’s simple-even hypothesis, retain its condition
\[
\delta_N(v_{\lambda,N})=1.
\]

Set
\[
B_{\lambda,N}
=
A_{\lambda,N}-\epsilon_{\lambda,N}I.
\]

The source constructs its positive quotient using \(B_{\lambda,N}\). In your original split formulation, that quotient is
\[
q_N:E_N(\lambda)^\tau
\longrightarrow
\bigl(E_N(\lambda)/\mathbb Cv_{\lambda,N}\bigr)^\tau.
\]

Two supported vectors are related exactly when their difference belongs to \(\mathbb Cv_{\lambda,N}\); \(\tau\) remains its own class.

The complete form identity is
\[
\boxed{
QW_\lambda(f,g)
=
\overline B_{\lambda,N}(q_Nf,q_Ng)
+
\epsilon_{\lambda,N}
\langle f,g\rangle_{L^2(du/u)}.
}
\]

This is where the original quotient has to remain in the argument.

Indeed,
\[
QW_\lambda(v_{\lambda,N},g)
=
\epsilon_{\lambda,N}\langle v_{\lambda,N},g\rangle.
\]
Therefore the unshifted form descends through this particular quotient precisely when
\[
\epsilon_{\lambda,N}=0.
\]

The shifted form descends because
\[
B_{\lambda,N}v_{\lambda,N}=0.
\]
The paper proves self-adjointness using that shifted form. fileciteturn148file7L85-L113

The replacement is **not to forget the unshifted form**. It is to retain the displayed pair:
\[
\bigl(\overline B_{\lambda,N},
\ \epsilon_{\lambda,N}\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\bigr).
\]

At the distribution level, the correction has an equally explicit location. Since
\[
QW(f,g)=\Psi(f^**g),
\qquad
(f^**g)(1)=\langle f,g\rangle,
\]
the shift is
\[
\boxed{\Psi\longmapsto\Psi-\epsilon_{\lambda,N}\delta_1.}
\]

Thus there is a particular arithmetic term to control. It is not removed by saying that the resulting null vector is supported.

## 4. Carry the original theta quotient into that finite comparison

This is the new comparison that makes the preceding discussion operational.

Keep the existing source-labelled quotient
\[
\mathfrak Q_W=\mathscr B/\Theta W,
\]
where \(W\) is a finite-dimensional space of admitted theta inputs. The supported carrier remains
\[
\{\tau\}\sqcup\bigsqcup_{W\ne0}\{W\}\times\mathfrak Q_W.
\]

In particular,
\[
e(W,[F])=(W,[0]),
\qquad
\tau(W,[F])=\tau,
\]
and transport from \(W\) to \(W'\) retains its calculated kernel
\[
\Theta W'/\Theta W.
\]
These are the original quotient relations in the workbench, not labels attached after arithmetic reflection. fileciteturn150file0L2-L5

Define the actual truncation map
\[
\boxed{
T_{\lambda,N}
=
\Pi_{\lambda,N}P_\lambda C:
\mathscr B\longrightarrow E_N(\lambda),
}
\]
where
\[
CF(u)=u^{1/2}F(u),
\]
\(P_\lambda\) restricts to \([\lambda^{-1},\lambda]\), and \(\Pi_{\lambda,N}\) is the paper’s orthogonal Fourier projection.

The half-density map has inverse \(C^{-1}f(u)=u^{-1/2}f(u)\), and
\[
\widehat{CF}(z)=\mathcal MF\!\left(\tfrac12-iz\right).
\]
This is the paper’s explicit Mellin–Fourier passage. fileciteturn148file7L390-L423

At each original support label, put
\[
R_{W,\lambda,N}=T_{\lambda,N}(\Theta W),
\qquad
L_{\lambda,N}=\mathbb Cv_{\lambda,N}.
\]

The quotient-compatible map is
\[
\boxed{
\mathscr B/\Theta W
\longrightarrow
E_N/R_{W,\lambda,N},
\qquad
[F]\longmapsto[T_{\lambda,N}F].
}
\]

The comparison with the paper’s quotient is then
\[
E_N/R_{W,\lambda,N}
\longrightarrow
E_N/(R_{W,\lambda,N}+L_{\lambda,N})
\longleftarrow
E_N/L_{\lambda,N}.
\]

Its two kernels are exactly
\[
L_{\lambda,N}/(L_{\lambda,N}\cap R_{W,\lambda,N})
\]
and
\[
R_{W,\lambda,N}/(R_{W,\lambda,N}\cap L_{\lambda,N}).
\]

**Those kernels are the retained discrepancy between the arithmetic relation and the finite ground-state relation.**

To retain it without prematurely killing either side, use the linear relation
\[
\boxed{
\mathfrak C_{W,\lambda,N}
=
\left\{
\bigl([F]_{\Theta W},[T_{\lambda,N}F]_{L_{\lambda,N}}\bigr):
F\in\mathscr B
\right\}.
}
\]

Its output fibre at any input is a translate of
\[
\boxed{
R_{W,\lambda,N}/(R_{W,\lambda,N}\cap L_{\lambda,N}).
}
\]

This follows by replacing \(F\) with \(F+\Theta\phi\), \(\phi\in W\). It states precisely when the correspondence is single-valued and precisely what information remains when it is not. The split lift retains \(W\) throughout and sends external absence to external absence.

This is the place to study your higher supported information against the spectral approximation—not an assertion that both quotients have already become isomorphic.

## 5. The discrepancy has a quantitative test on an actual arithmetic relation

Use the established theta input
\[
\phi_*(x)
=
(4\pi^2x^4-6\pi x^2)e^{-\pi x^2}.
\]

Define
\[
K=C\Theta(\phi_*/2).
\]
The factor \(1/2\) retains the passage from the full nonzero-integer sum to the positive-integer sum. Its transform is exactly
\[
\widehat K(z)=\Xi(z).
\]

Now take the label \(W_*=\mathbb C\phi_*\), and set
\[
u_{\lambda,N}
=
\Pi_{\lambda,N}P_\lambda K.
\]

The original arithmetic relation becomes the supported zero in \(\mathfrak Q_{W_*}\). Its image in the finite ground-line quotient is the class
\[
[u_{\lambda,N}]_{E_N/L_{\lambda,N}}.
\]

Define, without changing the source’s eigenvector,
\[
b_{\lambda,N}
=
\frac{\langle v_{\lambda,N},u_{\lambda,N}\rangle}
{\langle v_{\lambda,N},v_{\lambda,N}\rangle},
\]
and retain the spectral gap
\[
g_{\lambda,N}
=
\operatorname{dist}\!\left(
\epsilon_{\lambda,N},
\operatorname{Spec}(A_{\lambda,N})
\setminus\{\epsilon_{\lambda,N}\}
\right).
\]

At a simple lowest eigenvalue, expansion in the orthogonal eigenspaces gives
\[
\boxed{
\|u_{\lambda,N}-b_{\lambda,N}v_{\lambda,N}\|
\le
\frac{
\|(A_{\lambda,N}-\epsilon_{\lambda,N}I)u_{\lambda,N}\|
}{
g_{\lambda,N}
}.
}
\]

This is an estimate for the discrepancy of the **actual arithmetic relation**, not an arbitrary trial quotient.

For \(0\le a<1/2\), Fourier evaluation on the interval has the exact bound
\[
|\widehat f(z)|\le C_{\lambda,a}\|f\|,
\qquad |\Im z|\le a,
\]
where
\[
C_{\lambda,a}^2=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{\lambda^{2a}-\lambda^{-2a}}{2a},&a>0,\\[2mm]
2\log\lambda,&a=0.
\end{cases}
\]

Let the explicit omitted tail be
\[
T_\lambda(a)
=
\int_{(0,\lambda^{-1})\cup(\lambda,\infty)}
|K(u)|\max(u^a,u^{-a})\,\frac{du}{u}.
\]

Then the complete comparison is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{|\Im z|\le a}
\left|
b_{\lambda,N}\widehat v_{\lambda,N}(z)-\Xi(z)
\right|
\le{}&
T_\lambda(a)\\
&+C_{\lambda,a}\left(
\|(1-\Pi_{\lambda,N})P_\lambda K\|
+
\frac{
\|(A_{\lambda,N}-\epsilon_{\lambda,N}I)u_{\lambda,N}\|
}{
g_{\lambda,N}
}
\right).
\end{aligned}
}
\]

The theta tail tends to zero. At a fixed \(\lambda\), Fourier completeness controls the projection tail. **The uniform residual-to-gap estimate is the nontrivial term left in this explicit comparison.**

The source’s prolate-wave construction is directly relevant to estimating that term. Its §8 asks for the simple-even property and a sufficiently accurate comparison between the prolate-based trial function and the lowest eigenfunction of \(QW_\lambda\). The formula above attaches that question to our original arithmetic relation and its supported residual class. citeturn972558view0

## 6. The previous origin-jet work now has a specific role

The coordinate map is
\[
\sigma:\mathbb C_z\to\mathbb C_s,
\qquad
\sigma(z)=\tfrac12-iz,
\qquad
\sigma^{-1}(s)=i(s-\tfrac12).
\]

It gives
\[
\sigma^*(2\xi)=2\Xi,
\qquad
\sigma^*(s(1-s))=z^2+\tfrac14.
\]

Therefore the original support-preserving endpoint family becomes
\[
\boxed{
G\!\left(\mathcal O_s/(2\xi[s(1-s)]^m)\right)
\xrightarrow{\sim}
G\!\left(\mathcal O_z/(2\Xi[z^2+\tfrac14]^m)\right).
}
\]

The additional endpoint jets occur at
\[
z=-i/2,\qquad z=i/2.
\]

These are exactly the evaluation points in the paper’s polar term
\[
W_{0,2}(F)=\widehat F(i/2)+\widehat F(-i/2).
\]
fileciteturn148file7L471-L479

That locates the preceding work: it retains the endpoint sector accompanying the middle arithmetic factor. The new estimate in §5 addresses the comparison with that middle factor. The scalar \(\tau\) remains fixed under every displayed quotient map.

## 7. The primary target is a lower bound, not another support theorem

For the positivity route, the paper gives
\[

[**Cohomology and Lefschetz calculation**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Lefschetz_Cohomology_Return/index.html) · [**LaTeX**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Lefschetz_Cohomology_Return/CONTINUATION.tex) · [**Calculation package**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Lefschetz_Cohomology_Return_2026-09-11.zip)

## 1. What the trace does in the Weil proof

For a separated scheme \(X_0/\mathbb F_q\) of finite type and a constructible \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-sheaf \(\mathcal F_0\), with \(\ell\nmid q\), the Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula is
\[
\sum_{x\in X_0(\mathbb F_{q^n})}
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left((F_q^*)^n\mid\mathcal F_{\bar x}\right)
=
\sum_i(-1)^i
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left((F_q^*)^n\mid H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\right).
\]

It gives the determinant identity
\[
L(X_0,\mathcal F_0,T)
=
\prod_i
\det\!\left(1-TF_q^*\mid H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\right)^{(-1)^{i+1}}.
\]

Thus **the Euler product and the cohomological operators are linked by a theorem**, not by choosing an operator whose determinant already equals the desired function. This is SGA \(4\frac12\), Exposé II, §3. citeturn124749search2

For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve, constant coefficients give
\[
Z(X_0,T)
=
\frac{\det(1-TF_q^*\mid H^1)}
{(1-T)(1-qT)}.
\]

Purity then controls the eigenvalues of this already-identified \(H^1\). That is where the estimate belongs.

## 2. Put the correspondence on the original supported cohomology

Keep
\[
S=G(\mathbb C),\qquad e=0_{\mathbb C}\in S,\qquad 0_S=\tau.
\]

For a fixed-support diagram of complexes \(C_\lambda^\bullet\), the original reconstructed differential is
\[
\widetilde d(\lambda,x)=(\lambda,d_\lambda x).
\]

Its square is the supported zero:
\[
\widetilde d^{\,i+1}\widetilde d^{\,i}(\lambda,x)
=
(\lambda,0),
\]
not the constant map to external absence.

With \(\epsilon(y)=ey\), the original operations give
\[
Z_{\mathrm{sp}}^i
=
\operatorname{Eq}(\widetilde d^{\,i},\epsilon\widetilde d^{\,i}),
\]
followed by the support-preserving boundary quotient
\[
\boxed{
H_{\mathrm{sp}}^i
=
\bigsqcup_{\lambda}
\ker d_\lambda^i/\operatorname{im}d_\lambda^{i-1}.
}
\]

This is the coequalizer construction in the workbench, with its actual fibre transports. It retains
\[
e(\lambda,[x])=(\lambda,[0]),
\qquad
\tau(\lambda,[x])=(0_L,[0]).
\]
fileciteturn155file0L2-L2

### A necessary calculation: does the correspondence preserve the relations?

For the theta complex, use the existing
\[
V=
\{\phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R):
\phi\text{ even},\ \phi(0)=\widehat\phi(0)=0\},
\]
and
\[
\Theta\phi(t)=\sum_{n\ne0}\phi(nt).
\]

At an admitted source label \(W\subset V\), the degree-one fibre is
\[
Q_W=\mathscr B/\Theta W.
\]

For
\[
h\in\mathcal A=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R_{>0}),
\]
define the correspondence operator
\[
H_hF(t)
=
\int_0^\infty h(a)F(t/a)\,\frac{da}{a}.
\]

Directly,
\[
H_h\Theta=\Theta H_h.
\]

But this alone does not make \(H_h\) an endomorphism of every \(Q_W\): its source relations must be invariant. The framework supplies an explicit replacement. Retain \(W\) and its map into
\[
\boxed{
W^{\mathcal A}
=
W+\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}
\{h*\phi:h\in\mathcal A,\ \phi\in W\}.
}
\]

Associativity proves
\[
H_kW^{\mathcal A}\subseteq W^{\mathcal A},
\qquad
(W^{\mathcal A})^{\mathcal A}=W^{\mathcal A},
\]
and
\[
(W+U)^{\mathcal A}=W^{\mathcal A}+U^{\mathcal A}.
\]

The original transition is retained:
\[
Q_W\longrightarrow Q_{W^{\mathcal A}},
\qquad
\ker=
\Theta W^{\mathcal A}/\Theta W.
\]

We therefore obtain the genuine chain endomorphism
\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{ccc}
W^{\mathcal A}&\xrightarrow{\Theta}&\mathscr B\\
H_h\downarrow&&\downarrow H_h\\
W^{\mathcal A}&\xrightarrow{\Theta}&\mathscr B,
\end{array}
}
\]
and its induced supported cohomology action
\[
\boxed{
(W^{\mathcal A},[F])
\longmapsto
(W^{\mathcal A},[h*F]).
}
\]

**The additional relations needed to define the action have an explicit kernel. They are not silently discarded.**

## 3. Compute the trace of this action through the actual spectral maps

Retain the established Mellin identity
\[
\mathcal M\Theta\phi=2\xi H_\phi,
\qquad
\mathcal MF(s)=\int_0^\infty F(t)t^s\,\frac{dt}{t},
\]
where \(H_\phi\) is entire and the actual source function \(\phi_*\) has \(H_{\phi_*}=1\). Thus the analytic image ideal is \((2\xi)\). This is the existing theta-image calculation, not a new assumed spectral identification. fileciteturn155file0L2-L2

For a finite set \(Z\) of actual zeros, retaining their multiplicities, put
\[
A_Z=
\bigoplus_{\rho\in Z}
\mathbb C[z_\rho]/(z_\rho^{m_\rho}).
\]

The existing jet map is
\[
J_Z[F]
=
\left(
\sum_{j<m_\rho}
\frac{(\mathcal MF)^{(j)}(\rho)}{j!}z_\rho^j
\right)_\rho.
\]

Convolution gives the exact intertwiner
\[
\boxed{
J_ZH_h
=
M_{j_Z(\mathcal Mh)}J_Z,
}
\]
where the right side is multiplication in \(A_Z\).

On the basis
\[
1,z_\rho,\ldots,z_\rho^{m_\rho-1},
\]
this multiplication operator is triangular with diagonal entry \(\mathcal Mh(\rho)\). Hence
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Tr}(H_h\mid A_Z)
=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}m_\rho\,\mathcal Mh(\rho).
}
\]

Equivalently,
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Tr}(H_h\mid A_Z)
=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
\operatorname{Res}_{s=\rho}
\left(
\mathcal Mh(s)\frac{\xi'(s)}{\xi(s)}\,ds
\right).
}
\]

The local factorization
\[
2\xi(\rho+z)=u_\rho(z)z^{m_\rho}
\]
retains the actual unit \(u_\rho\). Its logarithmic derivative is holomorphic; the residue comes from \(m_\rho\,dz/z\).

The full nilpotent jet stays in the module and its operator. The scalar trace forgets its off-diagonal entries through the displayed trace map.

The supported version is still
\[
(W,[F])\longmapsto(W,J_ZF),
\]
with internal kernel
\[
(\ker J_Z)/\Theta W.
\]

A zero trace or zero spectral observation therefore does not turn the input into \(\tau\).

## 4. The two endpoint contributions also come from actual maps

Before imposing the two theta conditions, there is the exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow V
\longrightarrow\mathcal S(\mathbb R)^{\mathrm{even}}
\xrightarrow{m}
E_0\oplus E_1
\longrightarrow0,
\]
where
\[
m(\phi)=
\left(\phi(0),\int_{\mathbb R}\phi(x)\,dx\right),
\qquad
E_0=E_1=\mathbb C.
\]

Surjectivity is explicit: the functions
\[
g_0(x)=e^{-\pi x^2},
\qquad
g_2(x)=2\pi x^2e^{-\pi x^2}
\]
have moment columns \((1,1)\) and \((0,1)\).

For
\[
U_aF(t)=F(t/a),
\]
which is the earlier operator \(R_{a^{-1}}\),
\[
\mathcal MU_a=a^s\mathcal M,
\qquad
\boxed{
mU_a=
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&a\end{pmatrix}m.
}
\]

Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{Tr}(H_h\mid E_0)=\mathcal Mh(0),
\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}(H_h\mid E_1)=\mathcal Mh(1).
\]

These are the two polar representations. Their split lift carries a supported zero-input function to the supported vector \((0,0)\), not to external absence.

Combining them with the middle spectral trace gives
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal L_\Theta(h)
=
\mathcal Mh(0)
-\sum_\rho m_\rho\mathcal Mh(\rho)
+\mathcal Mh(1).
}
\]

The supplied paper’s explicit formula identifies this as
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal L_\Theta(h)
=
\sum_p\mathcal W_p(h)+\mathcal W_{\mathbb R}(h),
}
\]
with
\[
\mathcal W_p(h)
=
\log p\sum_{n\ge1}
\left(h(p^n)+p^{-n}h(p^{-n})\right)
\]
and
\[
\mathcal W_{\mathbb R}(h)
=
(\log4\pi+\gamma)h(1)
+
\int_1^\infty
\frac{
h(x)+x^{-1}h(x^{-1})-2x^{-1}h(1)
}{
x-x^{-1}
}\,dx.
\]

**Both endpoint terms, the sign of the middle trace, every prime-power contribution, and the archimedean subtraction remain present.** These are equations (3.1)–(3.4) of the supplied *Zeta Spectral Triples* TeX. fileciteturn151file7L331-L381

For these compactly supported smooth tests, the spectral sum is absolutely convergent. Here it is obtained as the limit of the calculated finite spectral traces—not asserted to be an ordinary trace of every infinite semimodule quotient.

Connes–Consani–Marcolli supply the established cyclic-homology realization: the restriction morphism from the adelic class space to the idelic class group produces a cokernel in cyclic modules, and its cyclic homology carries the action whose trace is the explicit formula. That is the source theorem connecting this arithmetic distribution to cohomology. citeturn124749academia22

The \(E_0,E_1\) above are the moment representations actually calculated here. Their realization as global degree-zero and degree-two cohomology of the richer split-support geometry has not been established merely by writing the alternating trace.

## 5. Where the estimate belongs in this construction

The relevant Weil II statement remains
\[
H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\twoheadrightarrow
I^i
\hookrightarrow H^i(X,\mathcal F),
\]
with
\[
\operatorname{weights}H_c^i\le w+i,
\qquad
\operatorname{weights}H^i\ge w+i.
\]

These force purity of **the same image** \(I^i\). The lower statement comes through
\[
\boxed{
H^i(X,\mathcal F)
\cong
H_c^{2d-i}(X,\mathcal F^\vee)^\vee(-d),
}
\]
not from changing the sign of a computed matrix. The inspected statements are retained in the package’s [Weil II TeX excerpt](sandbox:/mnt/data/Lefschetz_Cohomology_Return/sources/excerpt_deligne_en_witness.tex).

For the arithmetic action above, the corresponding quadratic trace is obtained by the actual involution
\[
h^\dagger(x)=x^{-1}\overline{h(x^{-1})}.
\]
It satisfies
\[
\mathcal M(h^\dagger*k)(s)
=
\overline{\mathcal Mh(1-\bar s)}\,\mathcal Mk(s).
\]

Thus the Weil pairing is a trace of a specified convolution action on the same spectral realization. Its positivity is the arithmetic endpoint in the Connes cohomological formulation. citeturn124749search1

The Chen–Moriwaki degree estimates may help construct geometric control, but that book explicitly introduces Arakelov degree as a **candidate replacement for an Euler–Poincaré characteristic** in its setting. It does not, by that construction alone, supply the required equivariant Lefschetz trace. fileciteturn151file0L305-L335

**So the main calculation is cohomological: retain the original quotient, put the correspondence action on it, identify its Lefschetz trace, and establish the duality that controls its middle image.** The finite-matrix lower bound is then a consequence or diagnostic of that structure—not a substitute for it.

\[

\tau_N,&a=b=\tau,\\[1mm]

where \(p:G(R)\to R\) is the arithmetic projection.

Now take your original quotient:
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde H_m^1
=
\operatorname{coeq}_{G(R)\text{-}\mathrm{SMod}}
(\widetilde d_m,\epsilon_N\widetilde d_m),
\qquad \epsilon_N(y)=ey.

### Calculate all three supported fibres

B_{-,m}=(gV_m),\qquad

(\{+,-\},gf),

\[
\ker\!\left(R/(gs^m)\to R/(g)\right)
=

Retain the workbench’s operators and source:
\[

\qquad

=

\[

\qquad
\widehat{\phi_*}=\phi_*.

These are the established differentiated-theta inputs, including their endpoint conditions. fileciteturn161file0L2-L2

For finite source labels, set
\[

\qquad
W^-_{m,N}=(1-D)^m\mathbb C[D]_{\le N}\phi_*.

\[

\longrightarrow

\qquad
[F]\longmapsto[(1-D)^mF].

\[

\xrightarrow{\;c_m\;}

=

### Substitute the comparison into the pairing

\[
\boxed{
\mathscr R_{m,Z}(f,c_mh)
=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
\operatorname{Res}_{s=\rho}
\frac{f^\dagger(s)h(s)}{g(s)}\,ds.
}
\]

This proves
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{im}c_m=(\ker c_m)^\perp.
}
\]

Containment follows by substituting \(f=ga\). Perfectness and the dimensions in the exact sequence give equality.

**This is the nondegenerate duality induced on the actual intermediate image.** The origin-jet kernel has not been forgotten: it is paired with the opposite endpoint quotient.

Explicitly, with source kernel representative
\[
ga(s),\qquad a(s)=\sum_{i<m}a_is^i,
\]
and target endpoint representative
\[
k(s)=\sum_{j<m}b_j(s-1)^j,
\]
their pairing is
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{i+j=m-1}
(-1)^{i-m}\overline{a_i}b_j.
}
\]

That retains every jet order and every reflection sign.

### The weight-one duality factor is also calculated

For the source dilation
\[
U_aF(x)=F(x/a),
\]
Mellin gives multiplication by \(a^s\). Since
\[
(a^s)^\dagger=a^{1-s},
\]
we obtain
\[
\boxed{
\mathscr R_{m,Z}(U_af,U_ak)
=
a\,\mathscr R_{m,Z}(f,k).
}
\]

Writing \(L_1\) for the one-dimensional representation on which \(a\) acts by \(a\), this is the perfect equivariant pairing
\[
\boxed{
\overline{C_{m,Z}}\otimes O_{m,Z}\longrightarrow L_1.
}
\]

The scalar factor playing the duality role has therefore been obtained from the same comparison and the actual arithmetic action.

## 5. The arithmetic Weil trace is a specific contraction of that duality

On
\[
I_Z=\bigoplus_{\rho\in Z}\mathcal O_\rho/(g),
\]
define the Jacobian morphism
\[
\boxed{
J_g:I_Z\to I_Z,\qquad[h]\mapsto[g'h].
}
\]

The induced residue pairing on \(I_Z\) is
\[
\mathscr R_Z(f,h)
=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
\operatorname{Res}_{\rho}\frac{f^\dagger h}{g}\,ds.
\]

Now calculate:
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathscr R_Z(f,J_gh)
&=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
\operatorname{Res}_{\rho}
\left(f^\dagger h\,\frac{g'}g\,ds\right)\\
&=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
m_\rho\,\overline{f(1-\bar\rho)}\,h(\rho)\\
&=
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(M_{f^\dagger h}\mid I_Z\right).
\end{aligned}
}
\]

The second equality follows from the actual local equation
\[
g(\rho+z)=u_\rho(z)z^{m_\rho},
\qquad
\frac{g'}g=\frac{m_\rho}{z}+\frac{u_\rho'}{u_\rho}.
\]

Equivalently, define directly on the comparison
\[
\boxed{
P_m:C_m\to O_m,
\qquad[f]\mapsto[(1-s)^m g'f].
}
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
\mathscr R_{m,Z}(f,P_mh)
=
\operatorname{Tr}
\!\left(M_{(q_mf)^\dagger(q_mh)}\mid I_Z\right).
}
\]

This is a **specific morphism whose pairing is the actual finite Weil spectral pairing**, with the full multiplication trace and multiplicities. For Mellin transforms of the admissible convolution tests, it is the corresponding finite part of the explicit formula in the supplied spectral-triple paper. citeturn434802view1

At a zero of multiplicity \(r\),
\[
g'\equiv r\,u_\rho(z)z^{r-1}\pmod{z^r}.
\]
Thus \(J_g\) has kernel \((z)\) and image \((z^{r-1})\).

The perfect residue pairing retains the full jet module. The Jacobian contraction records its scalar trace. Applying your support-preserving quotient to \((z)\) leaves a supported reduced fibre; it does not turn that fibre into \(\tau\).

## 6. Where Deligne has now been applied—and where his theorem is not being assumed

Deligne’s Corollary 3.3.6 concerns an image
\[
H_c^i(X,\mathcal F)\twoheadrightarrow I^i
\hookrightarrow H^i(X,\mathcal F),
\]
whose source and target receive opposite weight bounds through duality. His derived formulation uses the actual dualizing complex and the exchange of \(Rf_!\) with \(Rf_*\). I used the supplied TeX passages for those operations; the original article is *La conjecture de Weil II*. citeturn434802view0

Here, those operations have been performed on the programme’s concrete relations:

\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{c}
\text{original mixed-support differential}\\
\widetilde d_m(a,b)
=
\bigl(J,\;gs^mp(a)-g(1-s)^mp(b)\bigr)
\\[2mm]\downarrow\\
C_m\xrightarrow{c_m}O_m
\\[2mm]\downarrow\\
\operatorname{im}c_m
\cong\mathcal O/(2\xi),
\qquad
\operatorname{im}c_m=(\ker c_m)^\perp
\\[2mm]\downarrow\;J_g\\
\text{the actual arithmetic Weil trace pairing}.
\end{array}
}
\]

The endpoint kernel has generalized dilation eigenvalue \(1\); the endpoint cokernel has generalized dilation eigenvalue \(a\). Their full jet ladders are paired by the anti-diagonal formula above. The arithmetic eigenvalues remain \(a^\rho\) on the intermediate image.

There is one unproved geometric identification: these analytic source and target modules have not been identified with the global \(H_c^1\) and \(H^1\) of a realization carrying Deligne’s two weight estimates. I have therefore **not** inferred purity from perfect duality or from the existence of the support. The calculation supplies the comparison and its duality, rather than substituting a restatement of the desired positivity.

The exact checker verifies the kernels, mixed masks, residue pairing, reflection signs, Jacobian contraction and interlevel maps on finite algebraic models. The general proofs and source-reading ranges are in the linked package; GitHub was not modified in this turn.

**The result is the explicit intermediate-image morphism and its trace-producing duality, calculated inside the original split-support relations.**

**The audit found an explicit change in cohomology at the Mellin-realization step, a missing distinction between two Frobenius operations, and several places where valid local calculations were described as more global than they were.**

The original split-zero quotient survives these findings. What needed repair was the chain of conclusions drawn from its later realizations.

I audited the uploaded 1,945-line transcript against nine retained calculation packages and reran ten of their mathematical checkers. The result is **33 claim records**, each with its status, corrected morphism, dependencies, counterfactual, and constructive continuation—not 33 claims that everything was wrong.

[**Full audit reader**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Zero_Programme_Audit/index.html) · [**Searchable correction ledger**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Zero_Programme_Audit/ledger.html) · [**Complete audit package**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Zero_Programme_Audit_2026-09-12.zip) · [**Corrected programme state**](sandbox:/mnt/data/Split_Zero_Programme_Audit/PROGRAMME_STATE.md)

## 1. The most consequential finding: Mellin realization creates a relation that was not present before

This is a calculation on the **actual theta inputs already used in the programme**.

Retain
\[
D=-x\partial_x,\qquad
\phi_*=(4\pi^2x^4-6\pi x^2)e^{-\pi x^2},
\qquad
g(s)=2\xi(s).
\]

Define
\[
b_+=\Theta(D\phi_*),\qquad
b_-=\Theta((1-D)\phi_*).
\]

The established identities give
\[
\mathcal Mb_+=sg,\qquad
\mathcal Mb_-=(1-s)g.
\]
Those are the source inputs used to construct the later mixed differential. fileciteturn166file0L89-L123

The functions \(b_+\) and \(b_-\) are linearly independent over \(\mathbb C\). A constant linear relation would imply
\[
g(s)\bigl(c_+s+c_-(1-s)\bigr)=0,
\]
and therefore \(c_+=c_-=0\).

Consequently, with \(\mathcal O=\mathcal O_{\mathbb C}\), the map
\[
\delta:\mathcal O^2\longrightarrow
\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathscr B,
\qquad
(a,b)\longmapsto a\otimes b_+-b\otimes b_-
\]
is injective.

Now apply the actual Mellin-evaluation morphism
\[
\beta:\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathscr B
\longrightarrow\mathcal O,
\qquad
h\otimes F\longmapsto h\,\mathcal MF.
\]

The composite is
\[
\beta\delta(a,b)=g\bigl(sa-(1-s)b\bigr).
\]

Thus
\[
\boxed{
\ker\delta=0,\qquad
\ker(\beta\delta)=\mathcal O(1-s,s).
}
\]

The explicit witness is
\[
\boxed{
z=(1-s)\otimes b_+-s\otimes b_-\ne0,
\qquad
\beta(z)=0.
}
\]

This means that the comparison
\[
[\mathcal O^2\xrightarrow{\delta}\mathcal O\otimes\mathscr B]
\longrightarrow
[\mathcal O^2\xrightarrow{\beta\delta}\mathcal O]
\]
has \(H^0=0\) on the first complex and \(H^0\cong\mathcal O\) on the second.

**The square commutes, but that raw comparison is not a quasi-isomorphism.** Describing its analytic image as though the whole preceding cohomology had been transported was too strong.

### The correction retains your split-zero datum

On the original joint support face, the lifted maps are
\[
\widetilde\delta(J,(a,b))
=
(J,a\otimes b_+-b\otimes b_-),
\]
\[
\widetilde\beta(J,B)=(J,\beta B).
\]

Therefore
\[
(\{+,-\},z)\longmapsto(\{+,-\},0).
\]

It becomes the **supported zero in that same face**, not \(\tau\).

So this is not an objection obtained by forgetting your support structure. It is additional supported relation data that my propagation argument needed to carry.

### The repaired continuation is an exact kernel complex

For the full theta source, retain
\[
\alpha(h\otimes\phi)=hH_\phi,\qquad
\beta(h\otimes F)=h\mathcal MF,\qquad
\delta=1\otimes\Theta,
\]
with
\[
\beta\delta=g\alpha.
\]

The corrected derived comparison is
\[
\boxed{
\mathscr K^\bullet
\longrightarrow
[\mathcal O\otimes V\xrightarrow{\delta}\mathcal O\otimes\mathscr B]
\longrightarrow
[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\times g}\mathcal O]
\longrightarrow
\mathscr K^\bullet[1],
}
\]
where
\[
\mathscr K^\bullet=
[\ker\alpha\xrightarrow{\delta}\ker\beta].
\]

Its degree-one term gives the exact sequence
\[
\boxed{
0\longrightarrow
\frac{\ker\beta}{\delta(\ker\alpha)}
\longrightarrow
\mathcal O\otimes(\mathscr B/\Theta V)
\longrightarrow
\mathcal O/(g)
\longrightarrow0.
}
\]

The earlier work had written down this quotient kernel, but had not consistently carried its cohomological consequences into the subsequent interpretation.

There is an important limit on this audit finding: the displayed \(z\) belongs to the subspace divided out in \(\ker\beta/\delta(\ker\alpha)\). **It does not, by itself, prove that this final kernel is nonzero.** It proves that the raw realization creates the stated relation and that its kernel complex must be accounted for.

The constructive alternative is precise: prove that complex acyclic, or retain its contribution to the action, duality, and trace. Neither alternative discards the programme.

## 2. A second finding uses the split zero in an essential way: the two Frobenius operations differ

The earlier construction defined an additive Frobenius lift on
\[
D_{A,n}=G(A)^n
\]
by
\[
(\Phi_q(a))_{qi\bmod n}
=
(-1_A)^{\lfloor qi/n\rfloor}a_i^q,
\]
with absent coefficients remaining absent. It proved compatibility with Frobenius on the arithmetic quotient. That statement survives. fileciteturn164file0L470-L535

But this lift must not be silently identified with taking the \(q\)-th power **inside the original split-support semiring**.

Take the exact example
\[
A=\mathbb F_5,\qquad n=3,\qquad x=(1,1,\tau).
\]

The declared additive lift gives
\[
\boxed{\Phi_5(x)=(1,\tau,4).}
\]

Multiplying \(x\) five times using the original mixed-support multiplication gives
\[
\boxed{x^{\star5}=(1,e_{\mathbb F_5},4).}
\]

The middle coefficient has zero arithmetic amplitude in both cases. But one is a supported zero and the other is absent.

This happens because binomial coefficients divisible by five become the supported scalar \(e_{\mathbb F_5}\), not the external additive identity \(\tau\).

Let \(P_q(x)=x^{\star q}\). The exact diagram is
\[
\boxed{
\pi\Phi_q=F_q\pi=\pi P_q.
}
\]

The types are:

\[
\Phi_q:D_{A,n}\to D_{A,n}
\quad\text{is the specified semiring homomorphism},
\]

\[
P_q:D_{A,n}\to D_{A,n}
\quad\text{is a pointed multiplicative-monoid homomorphism}.
\]

In the displayed example, \(P_5\) is not additive.

The comparison retaining the discrepancy is
\[
\boxed{
(P_q,\Phi_q):
D_{A,n}\longrightarrow D_{A,n}\times_BD_{A,n},
}
\]
in the pointed multiplicative-monoid category, where \(B=A[t]/(t^n+1)\).

**This is exactly information that ordinary arithmetic projection hides and your split construction retains.**

The correction is not to retract the defined additive lift or the finite-field coefficient calculation. It is to carry this comparison into any claim about Frobenius on the richer object. The pure weight-zero \(H^0\) of the finite étale amplitude scheme does not automatically describe both of these supported operations.

## 3. The latest intermediate-image calculation is valid—but its cohomological placement needed to stay explicit

Retain
\[
C_m=\mathcal O/(gs^m),\qquad
O_m=\mathcal O/(g(1-s)^m),
\]
and
\[
c_m:C_m\to O_m,\qquad
[f]\longmapsto[(1-s)^mf].
\]

The exact sequence remains
\[
\boxed{
0\to\mathcal O/(s^m)
\xrightarrow{\times g}C_m
\xrightarrow{c_m}O_m
\to\mathcal O/((1-s)^m)\to0.
}
\]

Its arithmetic image is still
\[
I=\mathcal O/(g),
\]
through
\[
C_m\xrightarrow{q_m}I\xrightarrow{\kappa_m}O_m,
\qquad
\kappa_m[f]=[(1-s)^mf].
\]

These are valid module maps, with valid \(G(\mathcal O)\)-linear split lifts. They are not asserted to be unital ring homomorphisms. The retained calculation establishes exactly these kernels, image, and cokernel. fileciteturn166file0L125-L176

However, for the two-term complex in degrees zero and one,
\[
\boxed{
H^0[C_m\to O_m]=\mathcal O/(s^m),\qquad
H^1[C_m\to O_m]=\mathcal O/((1-s)^m).
}
\]

The arithmetic \(I\) is **the image**, not either cohomology group.

On finite spectral truncations, its contribution cancels from the alternating trace of that complex. Under dilation, the remaining endpoint supertrace is
\[
m(1-a).
\]

This point was already stated in the long LaTeX. My public framing did not keep it prominent enough in the working conclusion. The source explicitly says that the arithmetic image is not secretly the cohomology of this two-term complex. fileciteturn167file0L19-L23

The repair is to retain the two short exact sequences
\[
0\to E_{0,m}\to C_m\to I\to0,
\]
\[
0\to I\to O_m\to E_{1,m}\to0,
\]
and connect them to an actual global cohomological comparison. It is not to rename the image as \(H^1\).

## 4. The residue calculation survives, including an orientation sign that must never disappear

The reflection is
\[
\iota(\rho)=1-\bar\rho,
\]
and the germ map is
\[
\dagger:\mathcal O_{\iota(\rho)}\to\mathcal O_\rho,
\qquad
f\mapsto\overline{f(1-\bar s)}.
\]

It is conjugate-semilinear between reflected stalks. In local coordinates,
\[
\sum_j a_jz_{\iota(\rho)}^j
\longmapsto
\sum_j(-1)^j\bar a_jz_\rho^j.
\]

For the middle residue pairing,
\[
R_Z(f,h)=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}\operatorname{Res}_\rho
\frac{f^\dagger h}{g}\,ds,
\]
the exact identity is
\[
\boxed{\overline{R_Z(h,f)}=-R_Z(f,h).}
\]

The raw form is skew-Hermitian. Meanwhile,
\[
(g')^\dagger=-g',
\]
so the Jacobian morphism
\[
J_g[h]=[g'h]
\]
produces the Hermitian trace form
\[
\boxed{
Q_Z(f,h)=R_Z(f,J_gh)
=
\sum_{\rho\in Z}
m_\rho\,\overline{f(1-\bar\rho)}h(\rho).
}
\]

The original perfect pairing, the annihilator-image identity, and the Jacobian trace contraction remain valid. Their roles must not be merged into an unspecified “positive duality.” The original contraction and multiplicity formulas are retained in the preceding calculation. fileciteturn166file0L260-L298

Generator changes also remain explicit:
\[
R_{ug}(f,h)=R_g(f,u^{-1}h),
\qquad
J_{ug}=uJ_g\pmod g.
\]

In particular,
\[
R_{2\xi}=\tfrac12R_\xi,\qquad
J_{2\xi}=2J_\xi.
\]

The trace contraction is unchanged because both factors are carried, not because the factor two is declared irrelevant.

### The audit’s counterfactual test

For the unscaled test polynomial
\[
g_0(s)=(s-\tfrac14)(s-\tfrac34),
\]
the same formal comparison and residue machinery exist. On its two reduced stalks,
\[
R=
\begin{pmatrix}0&2\\-2&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
J=
\begin{pmatrix}-1/2&0\\0&1/2\end{pmatrix},
\]
so
\[
Q=RJ=
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]

For \(a=16\), dilation is \(U=\operatorname{diag}(2,8)\), and
\[
U^*QU=16Q,
\]
but
\[
(1,-1)Q(1,-1)^{\mathsf T}=-2.
\]

This is not a zeta counterexample. It establishes the exact scope of the formal lemma: **perfect duality and weight-one covariance alone do not force positivity**.

The constructive implication is to retain your richer data and identify the additional arithmetic-geometric property that excludes this behavior. It is not to conclude that the richer programme fails.

## 5. The repaired dependency graph no longer hides several tasks behind “one geometric identification”

My preceding answer said there was “one unproved geometric identification.” That description compressed several distinct requirements into one phrase. The same answer had correctly acknowledged that the local analytic modules were not yet the global compactly supported and ordinary cohomology carrying Deligne’s estimates. fileciteturn167file0L5-L15

The audited chain now retains:

\[
\boxed{
\begin{gathered}
\text{original split-support coefficients and relation diagram}\\
\downarrow\\
\text{actual theta complexes and correspondence action}\\
\downarrow\\
\text{Mellin realization \emph{with its kernel complex}}\\
\downarrow\\
\mathcal O/(2\xi)
\text{ and the endpoint comparison sequences}\\
\downarrow\\
\text{residue duality and Jacobian trace contraction}.
\end{gathered}
}
\]

The geometric continuation must preserve those objects through the compact-to-ordinary comparison, the correspondence action, the Lefschetz trace, the dualizing operation, and the tensor/weight estimates on the same image.

The following repairs are now part of the ledger, rather than qualifications left behind in older messages:

| Earlier passage | Audited replacement |
|---|---|
| Attach support labels to the final ordinary quotient. | Keep \(Q_W=\mathscr B/\Theta W\), with every transition kernel \(\Theta W'/\Theta W\). |
| Treat convolution saturation as another finite label. | Use the explicit map from finite labels to the larger invariant-subspace category, retaining the additional quotient kernel. |

The Rees length, symmetric-power amplification, graded-trace, endpoint-jet, and local residue calculations remain available. Their estimates stay attached to their actual input objects. They are no longer allowed to establish an assertion about a different arithmetic comparison without the intervening map.

## 6. The reproducibility audit found and repaired a real checker problem

All ten retained mathematical scripts passed when rerun normally.

Two of those scripts contained **33 Python `assert` statement sites**. Running with `python -O` removes those statements, while their success-reporting code still runs. Consequently, the earlier assertion that identical normal and optimized output demonstrated equivalent checking was not justified.

I made hardened copies replacing those assertions with explicit conditional exceptions. Both copies pass in normal and optimized modes. I then deliberately falsified a guard in each hardened copy: both modes correctly failed.

The original files were left unchanged; the audit package includes the diffs, hashes, old rerun outputs, hardened outputs, and deliberate-failure results.

An independent checker also passed **128 exact finite checks in eleven named suites**, including the new Frobenius-support discrepancy and the Mellin-relation example. These are regression checks of the encoded identities, not a substitute for the written analytic arguments.

## The corrected working conclusion

There are genuine calculations worth retaining. The audit does **not** replace them with another blanket retraction.

It does replace the claim that their composition had already preserved everything needed for Weil II. The important repaired object is now **the original supported complex together with the realization kernel, endpoint sequences, Frobenius comparison, and trace contraction**.
